_meta.notes: Per-venue facts generated by scripts/generate-venue-facts.ts using Claude with web search.

2028 Stadium.iconicMoments: SoFi Stadium opened in 2020 as the home of the NFL's Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers, and the Rams won Super Bowl LVI here in February 2022. It is set to host matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup and Super Bowl LXI in 2027 before the 2028 Games, where it will co-host the Opening Ceremony with the LA Memorial Coliseum and host the swimming competition.
2028 Stadium.spectatorExperience: An indoor-outdoor stadium under a translucent canopy roof, with open sides that let in the coastal breeze, sunk into the ground so most fans enter at mid-level. For swimming, fans look down on a 50-meter competition pool set on the stadium floor, with results and live footage on the huge double-sided, ring-shaped video board hanging above the field.
2028 Stadium.changes2028: Called "2028 Stadium" during the Games, the NFL stadium will have a temporary 50-meter pool built on its field, making it the largest swimming venue in Games history with about 38,000 seats, and the pool will be decked over for the Para Games opening ceremony.

Alamitos Beach Stadium.location: Alamitos Beach, Long Beach (next to downtown Long Beach)
Alamitos Beach Stadium.iconicMoments: A temporary stadium built for the 2028 Games on Alamitos Beach. It brings beach volleyball back to Southern California, where the sport began, and it is the first time the sport will be played at the Games in its home region. After the beach volleyball events, the venue will also host blind football (soccer) during the 2028 Para Games.
Alamitos Beach Stadium.spectatorExperience: An open-air stadium with temporary seating built on the sand of a wide beach, with the Pacific Ocean behind the court. Sessions run in the afternoon and evening, so later matches end around sunset, and downtown Long Beach is a short walk away.
Alamitos Beach Stadium.changes2028: Built as a temporary venue just for the 2028 Games on a public beach that normally has no stadium, and taken down afterward.

Belmont Shore.location: Belmont Shore waterfront near Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier, Long Beach
Belmont Shore.iconicMoments: Long Beach hosted the sailing events at the 1984 Los Angeles Games, and US Sailing later set up a training base in the city. For 2028 the Belmont Shore coastline is a mixed open-water zone, the site of the 10 km open water swims, coastal rowing, and the windsurfing and kite events.
Belmont Shore.spectatorExperience: This is an outdoor beach and ocean venue where fans watch from the shoreline and the area around Belmont Veterans Memorial Pier as races run on the water just offshore. Organizers picked the location partly because the coast suits spectator viewing, and the kite races, which decide the first sailing medals of the 2028 Games, are held close to the beach.
Belmont Shore.changes2028: A natural beachfront that will get temporary Games-only facilities for 2028, shared by open water swimming, coastal rowing and the board sailing events, while boat-class sailing takes place at the Port of Los Angeles.

Carson Center Court.location: Dignity Health Sports Park, Cal State Dominguez Hills campus, Carson
Carson Center Court.iconicMoments: The tennis stadium opened in 2003 as part of the Home Depot Center complex, and it hosted the LA Women's Tennis Championships. Venus and Serena Williams, Kim Clijsters and Maria Sharapova all played there. It also hosted the March 2005 Davis Cup first-round tie between the USA and Croatia. The complex is home to the USTA's high-performance training center, and the stadium has also hosted boxing and concerts.
Carson Center Court.spectatorExperience: Center Court is an open-air stadium with about 8,000 seats and 19 suites, so fans sit close to the court in the Southern California sun. It is one of several venues in a 125-acre sports complex that also includes the LA Galaxy's soccer stadium and the VELO Sports Center velodrome, about 14 miles south of downtown Los Angeles.
Carson Center Court.changes2028: Inside Dignity Health Sports Park, the tennis stadium will be called Carson Center Court during the Games and will host tennis, followed by wheelchair tennis the next month.

Carson Court 1.location: Dignity Health Sports Park, Cal State Dominguez Hills campus, Carson
Carson Court 1.iconicMoments: Carson Court 1 is a show court at Carson Courts, the tennis complex at Dignity Health Sports Park (opened 2003 as the Home Depot Center) that houses the USTA High-Performance Training Center. The complex's main stadium hosted the WTA's LA Women's Tennis Championships from 2003 to 2009 and a USA vs Croatia Davis Cup tie in March 2005. The 2028 Games will be the first time it hosts Games tennis.
Carson Court 1.spectatorExperience: An open-air outdoor court on a hard surface, smaller and closer to the action than the 360-degree Carson Center Court, so fans sit near the players in the Southern California summer sun. It is one of several courts in a walkable complex next to the LA Galaxy's soccer stadium.
Carson Court 1.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, the Carson Courts site combines permanent and temporary facilities, using Carson Center Court plus Courts 1 through 11 for tennis and, the following month, wheelchair tennis.

Carson Court 2.location: Dignity Health Sports Park, Carson (CSU Dominguez Hills campus), South Bay LA County
Carson Court 2.iconicMoments: Court 2 is a secondary court in the tennis center at Dignity Health Sports Park, which opened in 2003 as the Home Depot Center. The center's main 8,000-seat stadium has hosted pro tennis, boxing, concerts and the 2011 CrossFit Games, and the wider complex is home to MLS's LA Galaxy.
Carson Court 2.spectatorExperience: Court 2 is an open-air outdoor court that seats far fewer people than the main stadium, so fans sit close to the players in the midsummer Southern California sun. It sits in a sports complex shared with the soccer stadium, velodrome and hockey field.
Carson Court 2.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, the tennis center is renamed Carson Courts, and Court 2 is one of the courts used for tennis matches from July 19 to July 28.

Carson Courts 3-10.location: Dignity Health Sports Park complex, Carson, South Bay LA County
Carson Courts 3-10.iconicMoments: Courts 3-10 are outer courts at the tennis center of the Dignity Health Sports Park complex, which houses the USTA's High-Performance Training Center. The complex has hosted the WTA Tour's LA Women's Tennis Championships, Davis Cup ties, and USTA Pro Circuit events such as the Carson Challenger. 2028 will be the first time it hosts a Games event, with tennis followed the next month by wheelchair tennis.
Carson Courts 3-10.spectatorExperience: These are open-air outer courts with seating close to the court, so fans sit near the players and can walk between matches on different courts during early rounds. The 360-degree Center Court stadium sits in the same complex.
Carson Courts 3-10.changes2028: For the Games the Dignity Health Sports Park tennis complex is renamed Carson Courts, and it hosts all tennis matches from July 19 to 28, 2028.

Carson Field.location: Dignity Health Sports Park, Carson, South Bay LA County
Carson Field.iconicMoments: Carson Field is the track-and-field facility at Dignity Health Sports Park, a 125-acre training and competition complex that opened in 2003 on the Cal State Dominguez Hills campus. It is normally a training ground for the LA Galaxy and the home field of LA Galaxy II. The complex sits where the velodrome for the 1984 Los Angeles Games once stood. Hockey has no prior Games history at this site.
Carson Field.spectatorExperience: An open-air field venue where most of the seating will be temporary stands put up for the Games, with a primary pitch and a smaller secondary field. It sits right next to the LA Galaxy's soccer stadium, the tennis stadium and the indoor velodrome, so the area will be busy with fans from several sports at once.
Carson Field.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, the everyday training facility will be temporarily converted into a hockey venue with roughly 15,000 seats at the primary field and 5,000 at a secondary field, and it will host Para archery; organizers call it Carson Field instead of using its sponsor name.

Carson Stadium.location: Cal State Dominguez Hills campus, Carson, South Bay LA County
Carson Stadium.iconicMoments: Opened in 2003 as the Home Depot Center, the stadium hosted the 2003 FIFA Women's World Cup final and MLS Cup finals in 2003, 2004, 2008, 2011, 2012, 2014 and 2024. It has been home to the LA Galaxy since 2003, served as the NFL Chargers' temporary home from 2017 to 2019, and has staged international rugby sevens tournaments.
Carson Stadium.spectatorExperience: An open-air, soccer-specific stadium of about 27,000 seats in which every seat sits close to the field with clear sight lines. It is the main stadium of a larger sports complex that also includes a tennis stadium, a track-and-field facility and a velodrome.
Carson Stadium.changes2028: Dignity Health Sports Park is renamed Carson Stadium for the 2028 Games, and its main field will be set up first for rugby sevens (July 12-18) and then for archery (July 19-28), when compound archery makes its Games debut.

Carson Velodrome.location: Dignity Health Sports Park complex, Cal State Dominguez Hills campus, Carson
Carson Velodrome.iconicMoments: Opened in 2004, the velodrome is the national training center for USA Cycling's track program. It has hosted the 2004 UCI Junior Track World Championships, the 2005 UCI Track Cycling World Championships, the 2006-2008 UCI Track World Cups, the 2012 and 2017 UCI Para-cycling Track World Championships, and the 2024 Pan American Track Cycling Championships. It stands near the site of the now-demolished velodrome used for track cycling at the 1984 Los Angeles Games.
Carson Velodrome.spectatorExperience: It is an indoor arena seating about 2,450 around a 250-meter Siberian pine track that is 7 meters wide, with 45-degree banked turns where riders reach about 53 mph. The building is compact, so every seat is close to the track and has a clear view.
Carson Velodrome.changes2028: The venue normally operates as the VELO Sports Center (formerly the ADT Event Center) and will carry the name Carson Velodrome during the 2028 Games.

Comcast Squash Center.location: Universal Studios Lot, Universal City (San Fernando Valley, Los Angeles)
Comcast Squash Center.iconicMoments: Temporary venue that will host squash's first appearance in Games history, with men's and women's singles events. It is set on Courthouse Square, a Universal backlot set used in films including Back to the Future, To Kill a Mockingbird and Gremlins. It is also one of the first two venues in Games history to carry corporate naming rights, announced alongside Honda Center.
Comcast Squash Center.spectatorExperience: Spectators sit in temporary stands around squash courts installed on an open-air studio backlot, with the courthouse facade from Back to the Future and other film sets as the backdrop. Sessions such as the round of 16 run in the evening, roughly 7:30 to 11:15 pm.
Comcast Squash Center.changes2028: This working film backlot will be temporarily fitted with competition courts and spectator stands and branded as the Comcast Squash Center at Universal Studios for the 2028 Games.

DTLA Arena.location: South Park, Downtown Los Angeles (next to L.A. Live and the LA Convention Center)
DTLA Arena.iconicMoments: Opened as Staples Center on October 17, 1999. It is the home arena of the Lakers, Kings and Sparks, and the Clippers also played here until 2024. It has hosted several Lakers NBA championship runs and the Kings' Stanley Cup clincher in 2014. Kobe Bryant scored 81 points here in 2006 and 60 points in his final game in 2016, and the building is often called "The House That Kobe Built." It has hosted the Grammy Awards many times and held the 2009 Michael Jackson memorial.
DTLA Arena.spectatorExperience: This is an indoor, climate-controlled bowl with seating rising steeply on all sides of the floor, so even upper-level seats look straight down onto the competition area. It sits in the L.A. Live entertainment district, which has restaurants and plazas next door, and the Metro A and E lines stop nearby at Pico station.
DTLA Arena.changes2028: The arena is normally called Crypto.com Arena but will be renamed DTLA Arena for the Games because of sponsor naming rules, and it will be set up for artistic and trampoline gymnastics and the boxing finals.

Dodger Stadium.location: Chavez Ravine, Elysian Park, just north of Downtown Los Angeles
Dodger Stadium.iconicMoments: Dodger Stadium is the oldest MLB ballpark on the West Coast and has been home to the Los Angeles Dodgers since 1962. It hosted baseball as a demonstration sport at the 1984 Los Angeles Games, drawing an average of about 48,000 fans per game. It has hosted 11 World Series, most recently in 2024, as well as the 2017 World Baseball Classic final rounds, where the USA won the title.
Dodger Stadium.spectatorExperience: It is an open-air ballpark built into the hillside of Chavez Ravine, with tiered seating in its original 1962 pastel colors (yellow, light orange, sea-foam green and light blue). Upper decks look out over the Downtown LA skyline and the surrounding hills, and summer day and night games are played in the open air.
Dodger Stadium.changes2028: The ballpark has carried the naming-rights title "Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium" since March 2026, but Games announcements call it Dodger Stadium, and it is being used as an existing venue rather than rebuilt.

Energizer Park.location: Downtown West, St. Louis, Missouri (outside the LA area)
Energizer Park.iconicMoments: Built as a soccer-specific stadium, it opened on November 16, 2022 with a friendly between St. Louis City SC and Germany's Bayer Leverkusen, and it has been home to St. Louis City SC of MLS since the club's first season in 2023. The 2028 matches will be the first Games competition held in St. Louis since the city hosted the 1904 Games, the first held in the United States.
Energizer Park.spectatorExperience: An open-air downtown stadium with about 22,500 seats in a compact bowl designed to keep fans close to the pitch for a loud, tight atmosphere. It is the centerpiece of a 25.5-acre urban campus that also holds the club's headquarters and training fields, and the stadium opens out toward the surrounding district instead of facing only inward.
Energizer Park.changes2028: The stadium, called CityPark in 2023–2024 and renamed Energizer Park in 2025, will use the non-commercial name St. Louis Stadium during the 2028 Games, when it hosts men's and women's group-stage and knockout matches.

Etihad Park.location: Willets Point, Queens, New York City (next to Citi Field)
Etihad Park.iconicMoments: A new venue scheduled to open on July 17, 2027, as the home of MLS club New York City FC, which previously played at Yankee Stadium and Citi Field. It is New York City's first soccer-specific stadium and is billed as the first fully electric MLS stadium. It is one of several football venues outside Los Angeles for the 2028 Games, and NWSL champions Gotham FC will also move there starting in 2028.
Etihad Park.spectatorExperience: An open-air 25,000-seat stadium with a traditional soccer-specific seating bowl that keeps fans close to the pitch, under a transparent roof that lets daylight into the concourse and keeps crowd noise inside the bowl. Fans enter through "The Cube," a seven-story gateway covered in programmable LED screens, a short walk from the 7 train at Willets Point next to Citi Field.
Etihad Park.changes2028: For the 2028 Games the stadium is expected to go by the non-commercial name New York Stadium instead of its sponsor name.

Exposition Park Stadium.location: Exposition Park, South Los Angeles (next to the LA Memorial Coliseum)
Exposition Park Stadium.iconicMoments: Opened in April 2018 as the home of MLS club LAFC, it was the first open-air stadium built in the city of Los Angeles since Dodger Stadium in 1962. It sits on the former site of the Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena, and in 2022 it hosted the MLS Cup final, which LAFC won on penalties. It is also home to Angel City FC of the NWSL.
Exposition Park Stadium.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air, soccer-specific stadium with steep stands set close to the field and a canopy roof over the seating, so sight lines are tight and intimate. The 3,252-seat safe-standing supporters' terrace in the north end gives the stadium a loud, packed atmosphere.
Exposition Park Stadium.changes2028: The stadium is normally called BMO Stadium, but it will be renamed Exposition Park Stadium for the 2028 Games because of rules on sponsor names, and it will host flag football's debut at the Games and lacrosse's return.

Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium.location: Fairplex, Pomona, about 30 miles east of downtown Los Angeles
Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium.iconicMoments: The cricket ground was built at Fairplex, which has hosted the Los Angeles County Fair since 1922. Construction began with a groundbreaking in April 2026, and the ground is home to Major League Cricket's Los Angeles Knight Riders, joining the league schedule in its 2026 season. In 2028 it will stage cricket's return to the Games for the first time in 128 years, with men's and women's T20 tournaments.
Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium.spectatorExperience: An open-air oval cricket ground with roughly 10,000 seats set inside the large Pomona fairgrounds complex, so spectators sit close to the boundary under inland Southern California summer sun.
Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium.changes2028: Known day to day as the Knight Riders Cricket Ground, the venue will take the name Fairgrounds Cricket Stadium during the Games; organizers first planned a temporary, purpose-built structure at the Fairgrounds before the $21 million Knight Riders stadium was announced to serve as the cricket venue.

Galen Center.location: USC campus, Exposition Park area, Los Angeles
Galen Center.iconicMoments: Opened in October 2006 as the University of Southern California's first on-campus arena, it replaced the Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena as home of USC men's and women's basketball and volleyball. It has hosted WNBA Finals games in 2016, boxing and wrestling events, and the Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards six times. The 2028 Games will be its first time hosting Games competition.
Galen Center.spectatorExperience: An indoor, two-deck bowl of about 10,000 seats with 22 suites, small enough that seats sit fairly close to the floor, and windows on the north end look out toward downtown. The red-brick building stands at Figueroa Street and Jefferson Boulevard across from the USC campus, next to the Jefferson/USC Metro station, and a bust of Louis Galen stands on the street-level concourse.
Galen Center.changes2028: Under 2028 Games venue naming the arena is listed as the USC Sports Center, and it hosts badminton July 15-24 and rhythmic gymnastics July 27-29, followed by para badminton and wheelchair rugby.

Geodis Park.iconicMoments: Geodis Park opened on May 1, 2022, when Nashville SC played the Philadelphia Union in an MLS match. Nashville SC has played its home games there ever since. With about 30,109 seats, it is the largest soccer-specific stadium in the United States. In August 2023 it hosted the Leagues Cup final, where Lionel Messi's Inter Miami beat Nashville SC on penalties to win the first trophy in the club's history. It is one of six venues outside Los Angeles hosting early-round matches of the 2028 football tournaments, and Nashville is set to stage one of the first matches on July 10, 2028.
Geodis Park.spectatorExperience: Geodis Park is an open-air stadium built only for soccer. The design firm Populous enclosed the field with four stands that sit close to the pitch, and canopies cover much of the seating. A supporters' section with standing room adds steady crowd noise. The stadium is on the historic Nashville Fairgrounds site just south of downtown. Traffic and parking can back up on the surrounding streets after big matches.

Honda Center.location: Anaheim, Orange County (Katella Avenue, OCVIBE district)
Honda Center.iconicMoments: Opened in June 1993 as Anaheim Arena with a sold-out Barry Manilow concert, and was known as the Arrowhead Pond of Anaheim until 2006. It has been home to the NHL's Anaheim Ducks since 1993, and hosted the 2003 and 2007 Stanley Cup Finals; the Ducks won the Cup in 2007. The arena was also home to the LA Clippers part-time from 1994 to 1999, and in 2024 it hosted AVP pro beach volleyball on a sand court laid inside the arena.
Honda Center.spectatorExperience: An indoor, city-owned arena with an enclosed seating bowl wrapped around the floor, and air conditioning for the July sessions. It is the anchor of Anaheim's OCVIBE entertainment district, and longtime local fans still call it "The Pond."
Honda Center.changes2028: The arena will host every indoor volleyball match of the 2028 Games, from the preliminary rounds through the medal matches, between July 15 and July 30, 2028.

Industry Hills MTB Course.location: Industry Hills, City of Industry, San Gabriel Valley
Industry Hills MTB Course.iconicMoments: The cross-country course is being built for the 2028 Games and has no earlier Games or major mountain bike racing history. It sits in the Industry Hills recreation area, which was developed on a former refuse site around 1980. The area includes the Industry Hills Golf Club at Pacific Palms, which has hosted the California State Open since 1980, and the Industry Hills Expo Center, a former equestrian facility that opened in 1981.
Industry Hills MTB Course.spectatorExperience: The open-air, outdoor course is set into a hilltop in the San Gabriel Valley and winds over rough ground with turns, drops and jumps. Viewing areas along the course let spectators watch riders on technical sections, and they can move between points on the loop as riders pass several times.
Industry Hills MTB Course.changes2028: A new cross-country mountain bike course is being built in the Industry Hills grounds for the 2028 Games, probably on the land around the Industry Hills Expo Center and the equestrian center northwest of the golf course.

Intuit Dome.location: Inglewood, just south of SoFi Stadium
Intuit Dome.iconicMoments: Opened in August 2024 as the privately funded home of the NBA's LA Clippers, built for about $2 billion by team owner Steve Ballmer. It was chosen to host the 2026 NBA All-Star Game, and it will host the 5x5 basketball tournaments at the 2028 Games, its first time hosting a Games event.
Intuit Dome.spectatorExperience: This is an indoor arena built just for basketball. Its signature feature is "The Wall," 51 uninterrupted rows of seats at one end that hold about 4,500 of the loudest fans. Above the court hangs a two-sided halo video board covering nearly an acre, and the arena advertises the most legroom in the NBA plus a large outdoor plaza.
Intuit Dome.changes2028: The arena keeps the Intuit Dome name for the 2028 Games under a naming-rights sponsorship deal, after organizers had planned to call it the Inglewood Dome.

LA Convention Center Hall 1.location: South Figueroa Street, downtown Los Angeles (next to L.A. Live)
LA Convention Center Hall 1.iconicMoments: The Los Angeles Convention Center opened in July 1971 with the West Hall, designed by Charles Luckman. It served as the Main Press Center for the 1984 Los Angeles Games. It is better known as a large trade-show and fan-convention site in downtown LA than as a sports venue.
LA Convention Center Hall 1.spectatorExperience: This is an indoor exhibition hall fitted with temporary seating for about 7,000 people around the competition area. It is close to the Pico Metro station, the L.A. Live entertainment district and Crypto.com Arena, and other sports take place in other halls of the same complex.
LA Convention Center Hall 1.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, this normally flat-floor exhibition hall gets temporary seating and fields of play for fencing (July 15-23), taekwondo (July 26-29), wheelchair fencing and para taekwondo.

LA Convention Center Hall 2.location: Downtown Los Angeles, next to L.A. Live and the DTLA Arena
LA Convention Center Hall 2.iconicMoments: The Los Angeles Convention Center opened on July 11, 1971; its first building, the West Hall, was originally named Yorty Hall after Mayor Sam Yorty. At the 1984 Games it served as the Main Press Center, not as a competition venue; that year judo was held elsewhere and wrestling took place at the Anaheim Convention Center. For 2028 it is one of the Games' busiest sites, with five sports spread across its halls.
LA Convention Center Hall 2.spectatorExperience: This is an indoor, climate-controlled exhibition hall in the downtown venue cluster within walking distance of L.A. Live and Metro's Pico station. Fans sit in temporary stands around the competition mats, and other sessions run in neighboring halls of the same building.
LA Convention Center Hall 2.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, the exhibition space is being temporarily turned into a competition venue with mats and spectator seating for judo and wrestling, while other halls host fencing, table tennis and taekwondo.

LA Convention Center Hall 3.location: Downtown Los Angeles, next to L.A. Live and Crypto.com Arena
LA Convention Center Hall 3.iconicMoments: The Los Angeles Convention Center opened in 1971 at 1201 S. Figueroa St. Charles Luckman designed it, and the West Hall (originally Yorty Hall) was the first section built. The center served as the press center for the 1984 Los Angeles Games. It is best known as the site of large LA events such as E3, Anime Expo, the LA Auto Show and other trade and consumer shows.
LA Convention Center Hall 3.spectatorExperience: This is an indoor, climate-controlled exhibit hall turned into a competition arena, so the atmosphere is close and fans sit near the tables, not in a large bowl. The International Table Tennis Federation president has said the venue is too small for the sport's demand, so seats may be limited.
LA Convention Center Hall 3.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, Hall 3 will be fitted with temporary seating and field-of-play equipment for table tennis, while other halls in the complex host fencing, judo, taekwondo and wrestling.

LA Memorial Coliseum.iconicMoments: Built as a memorial to Los Angeles veterans of World War I, the Coliseum was the main stadium for the 1932 and 1984 Summer Games, where it held the opening and closing ceremonies and track and field both times, and Carl Lewis won his four golds there in 1984. It will be the first stadium to hold ceremonies and track and field at three Summer Games. It also hosted the first AFC-NFC championship game, which later became the Super Bowl, and it is a National Historic Landmark.
LA Memorial Coliseum.spectatorExperience: The Coliseum is an open-air bowl with no roof, so fans sit in the Southern California summer sun. The main entrance is through the arched Peristyle plaza, where two bronze statues and the cauldron tower from past Games stand.
LA Memorial Coliseum.changes2028: The stadium was heavily refurbished in 2019, and a temporary track will be installed for 2028 in place of its normal USC football layout.

Long Beach Aquatics Center.location: Long Beach Convention Center lot, downtown Long Beach
Long Beach Aquatics Center.iconicMoments: A temporary venue built for the 2028 Games on the Long Beach Convention and Entertainment Center grounds, with no earlier sports history. It will host artistic swimming and water polo during the Games and para swimming afterward. Long Beach also hosts handball, rowing, canoe sprint, sailing, marathon swimming and triathlon in 2028.
Long Beach Aquatics Center.spectatorExperience: An open-air temporary stadium built around a competition pool, so spectators watch outdoors in Long Beach's coastal summer weather near the downtown waterfront.
Long Beach Aquatics Center.changes2028: Temporary Games-only structure built on the Long Beach Convention Center parking lot for the 2028 Games.

Long Beach Arena.iconicMoments: Long Beach Arena hosted the volleyball tournaments at the 1984 Los Angeles Games, which makes 2028 its second Summer Games. It has also hosted NCAA men's basketball tournament games, served for many years as the home court of Long Beach State basketball, and has been a regular stop for concerts and performances since it opened in 1962.
Long Beach Arena.spectatorExperience: The arena is an indoor, drum-shaped building designed by architect Kenneth Wing. It sits within the Long Beach Convention and Entertainment Center near the harbor. Its round exterior wall carries Wyland's "Planet Ocean" Whaling Wall, a 116,000-square-foot mural of gray whales and other local sea life that was once listed as the largest mural in the world.
Long Beach Arena.changes2028: The venue is set to be upgraded before the 2028 Games and will be configured for about 12,000 handball spectators.

Long Beach Climbing Theater.location: Long Beach Convention Center lot, downtown Long Beach waterfront
Long Beach Climbing Theater.iconicMoments: A temporary venue built only for the 2028 Games, with no previous sports history. It will host all climbing events (boulder, lead and speed) across six days, July 24-29, 2028. Climbing first appeared in the Games at Tokyo 2020 and is now a permanent part of the program.
Long Beach Climbing Theater.spectatorExperience: An open-air stadium with stands facing a temporary climbing wall and a large video screen, set on the Long Beach coast with the Pacific Ocean behind the wall. It is in the same Convention Center lot as the temporary venues for water polo, artistic swimming and target shooting, so several other sports are within walking distance.
Long Beach Climbing Theater.changes2028: A temporary climbing stadium and wall will be built in what is normally the Long Beach Convention Center parking lot and removed after the Games.

Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.location: Long Beach Convention Center, downtown Long Beach waterfront
Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.iconicMoments: The shooting hall is set up inside the Long Beach Convention Center, which hosted fencing at the 1984 Los Angeles Games. Rifle and pistol were moved here from the Prado shooting range in Chino, which hosted shooting in 1984. Organizers say 2028 will be the first Games where target shooting is held within walking distance of other sports.
Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.spectatorExperience: Spectators watch from inside a temporary indoor range with marked shooting lanes, set within a convention hall on the downtown waterfront. The hall sits in the Long Beach Zone, a short walk from the beach volleyball, aquatics, climbing and handball venues, so it is easy to visit more than one venue in a day.
Long Beach Target Shooting Hall.changes2028: A temporary indoor range will be built inside the Long Beach Convention Center for rifle and pistol events and shooting para sport, and the hall will carry the name Long Beach Target Shooting Hall during the Games.

Marine Stadium.location: Alamitos Bay, Long Beach (Belmont Heights / Belmont Shore area)
Marine Stadium.iconicMoments: Marine Stadium was the first man-made rowing course in the United States and was dredged and built to host the rowing events of the 1932 Los Angeles Games, where its width let four crews race side by side. It later hosted the 1968 and 1976 U.S. men's rowing trials and the 1984 U.S. women's rowing trials, and it is California Registered Historical Landmark No. 1014. Today it is a training and racing base for the U.S. national rowing team, Cal State Long Beach and the Long Beach Rowing Association, and it hosts the annual Long Beach Sprint Nationals speedboat races.
Marine Stadium.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air, saltwater course inside a long, narrow channel off Alamitos Bay. Spectators watch from the shoreline next to the racing lanes, with the Belmont Shore neighborhood, the beach and the downtown Long Beach skyline in view.
Marine Stadium.changes2028: For 2028 the course will host rowing over 1,500 meters instead of the usual 2,000 meters, plus canoe sprint, para rowing and para canoe. It is the venue's second time hosting the Summer Games and its first time hosting Para events.

OKC Softball Park.location: Northeast Oklahoma City, Oklahoma (about 1,300 miles from Los Angeles)
OKC Softball Park.iconicMoments: The stadium opened in 1987 as the Don E. Porter ASA Hall of Fame Stadium. It has hosted the NCAA Women's College World Series every year since 1990, and it has also hosted the World Cup of Softball and U.S. national team trials. It sits inside the USA Softball Hall of Fame Complex, next to the National Softball Hall of Fame and Museum, and is often called the "Mecca of Softball."
OKC Softball Park.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air, softball-only ballpark with two levels of seating close to the field and a large video board. Women's College World Series crowds there are known for being loud. Midsummer day games in Oklahoma are hot, and little of the seating is shaded because the upper deck covers only the last row or two below it.
OKC Softball Park.changes2028: The stadium, called Devon Park since 2024, is listed as OKC Softball Park for the 2028 Games, and a city-funded indoor practice facility and new shaded stadium entrance are being added next to it before 2028.

OKC Whitewater Center.location: Boathouse District on the Oklahoma River, just south of downtown Oklahoma City, Oklahoma
OKC Whitewater Center.iconicMoments: Opened in May 2016 as RIVERSPORT Rapids, a $45 million whitewater center paid for by Oklahoma City's MAPS 3 voter-approved sales tax, with a pumped channel that runs at about 1,200 to 1,400 cubic feet per second at full flow. The site hosted ICF World Ranking events in the lead-up to the 2028 Games and the 2026 ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships (July 20-25, 2026), the first slalom world championships held in North America in more than a decade. Oklahoma City was picked for canoe slalom because it already had a competition course, which saved the cost of building a temporary course in Los Angeles.
OKC Whitewater Center.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air course in the summer heat. Spectators watch from the banks of a 304.8 m concrete slalom channel that drops 5.15 m from start to finish, with the downtown OKC skyline behind it. The McClendon Whitewater Center building beside the course has a covered patio and two decks that look over the rapids on one side and the Oklahoma River on the other.
OKC Whitewater Center.changes2028: The venue normally operates as RIVERSPORT Rapids and the Aubrey K. McClendon Whitewater Center, and is called the OKC Whitewater Center for the 2028 Games. It is one of two Oklahoma City venues for the Games, about 1,200 miles from Los Angeles.

PayPal Park.location: Airport West site, North San Jose, next to San Jose International Airport (Bay Area, about 340 miles north of Los Angeles)
PayPal Park.iconicMoments: Opened in March 2015 as Avaya Stadium, a soccer-only stadium the San Jose Earthquakes paid for themselves. It ended a long stretch in which the club had no permanent home, after the original Earthquakes moved to Houston in 2005. In the first match, San Jose beat the Chicago Fire 2-1. It took the name PayPal Park in 2021, and the NWSL's Bay FC has also played there since 2024. In 2016 it hosted the MLS All-Star Game against Arsenal.
PayPal Park.spectatorExperience: This open-air stadium has the smallest capacity in MLS, so every seat is close to the field and the stands rise steeply, much like grounds in Europe. A roof covers much of the seating, and the stadium is known for its large outdoor bar behind one end. Planes landing at the airport next door pass over during matches.

Peacock Theater.location: L.A. Live, South Park, Downtown Los Angeles
Peacock Theater.iconicMoments: Opened in October 2007 as the Nokia Theatre and later renamed Microsoft Theater (2015-2023) before becoming the Peacock Theater, it is best known as a host of major award shows including the Primetime Emmy Awards, the American Music Awards, the ESPYs and the BET Awards. It has also staged concerts by artists such as Katy Perry, Ed Sheeran and Kelly Clarkson. The 2028 Games will be its first time hosting medal-level international sport.
Peacock Theater.spectatorExperience: An indoor, air-conditioned theater with about 7,100 seats in tiers facing one of the largest indoor stages in the United States, so spectators look straight at a single raised platform or ring instead of sitting around it as in an arena. It sits in the L.A. Live entertainment complex next to the DTLA Arena, with restaurants and plazas outside and the Pico Metro station nearby.

Port of Los Angeles.location: San Pedro Bay harbor, San Pedro and Wilmington, Los Angeles
Port of Los Angeles.iconicMoments: Los Angeles Harbor hosted the sailing regattas at the 1932 Games, so 2028 sailing returns to the same waters almost a century later. Most of the time it is a working container port, where large containerships, bulk carriers, tugs and pilot boats move through San Pedro Bay.
Port of Los Angeles.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air harbor venue. Spectators watch dinghy, skiff and multihull racing from the shore, against a backdrop of the working port. Organizers chose the site partly because people can watch the races from close by, which is uncommon for sailing.
Port of Los Angeles.changes2028: The working container port will become the main sailing venue for the 2028 Games and host six boat events: men's and women's dinghy, men's and women's skiff, mixed dinghy and mixed multihull. The board events will be held at nearby Belmont Shore in Long Beach.

Riviera Country Club.location: Pacific Palisades, Westside of Los Angeles
Riviera Country Club.iconicMoments: Riviera is a private club whose George C. Thomas Jr.-designed course has hosted the Los Angeles Open (now the Genesis Invitational, hosted by Tiger Woods) more than 60 times. Ben Hogan won the 1948 U.S. Open and several Los Angeles Opens here, which is why it is nicknamed "Hogan's Alley," and a statue of Hogan stands near the 18th green. The club also hosted equestrian events at the 1932 Los Angeles Games and the 2026 U.S. Women's Open.
Riviera Country Club.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air, walk-the-course venue set in a canyon off Sunset Boulevard, with fans spread along the fairways rather than in one central stand. The hillside clubhouse looks down on the 18th green, and the slopes around it form a natural amphitheater for the finishing holes. At the Genesis Invitational, fans usually park off-site and take a shuttle bus to the course.

Rose Bowl Aquatics Center.iconicMoments: The center opened in 1990 on the site of Pasadena's Brookside Plunge, a city pool built in 1923 and closed in 1984. Part of the reason for building it was Pasadena's diving history, including Dorothy Poynton, who won medals in diving. The pool has hosted training for the 2000 U.S. swimming and diving teams and the 2008 U.S. National Diving Championships.
Rose Bowl Aquatics Center.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air pool complex in the Arroyo Seco canyon, just south of the Rose Bowl Stadium, with two 50-meter pools and a diving well. Spectators watch outdoors in the Southern California summer with the hills of Brookside Park behind the pool.
Rose Bowl Aquatics Center.changes2028: In September 2025, diving was moved here from the John C. Argue Swim Stadium in Exposition Park because World Aquatics said that pool was not wide or deep enough, and the center's regular programs are scheduled to move out ahead of the Games so the venue can be prepared.

Rose Bowl Stadium.iconicMoments: The Rose Bowl hosted track cycling on a temporary track at the 1932 Games and the soccer tournament at the 1984 Games, where France beat Brazil 2-0 in the gold medal match before 101,799 fans. It also hosted the 1994 men's World Cup final, in which Brazil beat Italy on penalties, and the 1999 Women's World Cup final, in which the United States beat China on penalties in front of 90,185 fans. It is the home of the annual Rose Bowl Game and UCLA football, a U.S. National Historic Landmark, and in 2028 it joins the LA Memorial Coliseum as one of the first venues to host events at three different Summer Games.
Rose Bowl Stadium.spectatorExperience: It is an open-air elliptical bowl set low in the Arroyo Seco, with the San Gabriel Mountains in view behind the stands, and the 2028 men's and women's soccer semifinals and gold medal matches will be played on its natural-grass field. The historic bench-style seats have little legroom, and the sunny afternoons can be hot, so plan for sun exposure.
Rose Bowl Stadium.changes2028: The $80 million Lasting Legacy Campaign has already added a new sound system, a refurbished marquee and an east-side safe-standing section, and a South End Zone Field Club with about 800-900 seats is due in 2026. Before the Games this could reduce capacity slightly from 89,702, and further reductions to about 70,000-72,000 are planned after 2028.

Santa Anita Park.iconicMoments: Santa Anita Park opened in 1934 and is one of the main thoroughbred racetracks in the United States. It is home to the Santa Anita Derby, the Santa Anita Handicap and the American Oaks. Santa Anita also hosted the equestrian events at the 1984 Los Angeles Games, and Seabiscuit won the 1940 Santa Anita Handicap here.
Santa Anita Park.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air racetrack. Spectators sit in a historic grandstand that holds about 26,000, looking across the track and infield toward the San Gabriel Mountains, and the infield can take about 50,000 more. Outside racing season, the park also hosts large events such as the Enchant LA holiday light festival.

Scotts Miracle-Gro Field.iconicMoments: Opened on July 3, 2021 as Lower.com Field, the stadium replaced Historic Crew Stadium as home of the Columbus Crew of MLS. The Crew won the 2023 MLS Cup final against LAFC here. It hosted the 2026 NWSL Challenge Cup and will become home to Columbus's new NWSL club in 2028. For the 2028 Games it is one of seven US stadiums chosen to host men's and women's football tournament matches.
Scotts Miracle-Gro Field.spectatorExperience: An open-air, soccer-specific stadium of about 20,000 seats, with stands built close to the pitch and a roof canopy covering much of the seating; the Crew's supporters' section, the Nordecke, gives one end its noise. It is in the walkable Arena District, within walking distance of Columbus's other pro sports venues and downtown restaurants.
Scotts Miracle-Gro Field.changes2028: The venue took the ScottsMiracle-Gro Field name in 2025 after its first five seasons as Lower.com Field; for the 2028 Games it will host football matches far from the Los Angeles hub.

Snapdragon Stadium.location: Mission Valley, San Diego (about 120 miles south of Los Angeles)
Snapdragon Stadium.iconicMoments: Snapdragon Stadium opened in August 2022 on San Diego State University's Mission Valley campus. It is home to SDSU Aztecs football, San Diego Wave FC of the NWSL and San Diego FC of MLS, and has hosted the Holiday Bowl since 2024. San Diego Wave FC set an NWSL attendance record in its first match there on September 17, 2022, and San Diego FC's first home match in March 2025 drew the largest sports crowd in the stadium's history.
Snapdragon Stadium.spectatorExperience: Snapdragon Stadium is an open-air stadium with a natural Bermuda grass field and about 35,000 seats, and its compact bowl was designed for soccer, rugby and college football. For the 2028 Games it will host 11 men's and women's group-stage matches on July 11, 14 and 17, 2028.

Trestles State Beach.location: Just south of San Clemente, south Orange County, north of Camp Pendleton
Trestles State Beach.iconicMoments: Lower Trestles is a cobblestone A-frame break and one of the best-known high-performance waves in California. It has hosted many international pro events and U.S. national championships, and it has been the site of the World Surf League Finals, the one-day contest that decides the world titles. Filipe Toledo won the men's title there in 2022 and 2023, Stephanie Gilmore won the women's title in 2022, and Caroline Marks won it in 2023. San Clemente is also home to USA Surfing, the sport's national governing body.
Trestles State Beach.spectatorExperience: This is a natural, open-air beach inside a state park, so there are no permanent grandstands. Fans watch from the sand and cobblestone shore close to the lineup, and the setting feels like a local surf break rather than a stadium.
Trestles State Beach.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, temporary competition and spectator facilities will go up on the state beach, and on-site attendance will be capped well below the 6,000 to 7,000 people that regular pro events draw, so San Clemente is planning off-site viewing parties.

Valley Complex 1.location: Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, Encino, San Fernando Valley
Valley Complex 1.iconicMoments: Valley Complex 1 is a temporary venue built only for the 2028 Games. It sits in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, the second-largest urban park in Los Angeles, near where the 405 and 101 freeways meet. The 2028 Games will be the first time the San Fernando Valley has hosted events; it had none in 1932 or 1984. Bringing BMX here also returns the sport to its LA roots, since the first organized BMX race was held at Palms Park in West Los Angeles in 1969.
Valley Complex 1.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air, temporary venue with courses built for BMX Freestyle runs and Street Skateboarding. It is one of four complexes that make up a parkland sports zone with golf courses, picnic areas and wildlife areas. Some sessions, such as the men's street final, are scheduled for evening start times around 8:30 pm.
Valley Complex 1.changes2028: For the 2028 Games, part of the Sepulveda Basin park (17017 Burbank Blvd, Encino) will be temporarily turned into this complex, and the city is cleaning up the basin ahead of time.

Valley Complex 2.location: Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, San Fernando Valley, Los Angeles
Valley Complex 2.iconicMoments: Valley Complex 2 is a temporary venue built only for the 2028 Games. It has no prior Games or major sports history. It is one of four temporary Valley Complexes set up inside the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, which is Los Angeles' second-largest urban park. 2028 is the first time the San Fernando Valley will host Games competition.
Valley Complex 2.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air temporary venue inside a large city park that also has sports fields, golf courses, picnic areas and wildlife areas. It sits in the Valley Zone with the other complexes, which hold BMX, street skateboarding and 3x3 basketball, so fans can visit several sports in one trip.
Valley Complex 2.changes2028: The site is normally parkland and will be built up as a temporary competition venue for park skateboarding and modern pentathlon, then removed after the Games.

Valley Complex 3.location: Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, Encino, San Fernando Valley
Valley Complex 3.iconicMoments: Valley Complex 3 is a temporary venue built only for the 2028 Games and has no earlier competition history. It is one of four temporary complexes in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, a large city park in the west San Fernando Valley. Together with the other complexes, which host BMX, skateboarding and modern pentathlon, it marks the first time Games events will be held in the Valley.
Valley Complex 3.spectatorExperience: An open-air, temporary eight-sided stand built around a single 3x3 court, so fans watch from every side. The park setting has golf courses, sports fields and wildlife areas nearby, and some sessions run into the evening, including quarterfinals that start at 9 p.m.
Valley Complex 3.changes2028: This is a temporary structure for the 2028 Games only: an eight-sided 3x3 basketball stand built on open parkland in the Sepulveda Basin, which will be turned into a sports park called the Valley Zone for the Games.

Valley Complex 4.location: Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, Encino/Van Nuys, San Fernando Valley
Valley Complex 4.iconicMoments: A temporary venue built for the 2028 Games and one of four Valley Complexes in the Sepulveda Basin Recreation Area, the second-largest urban park in Los Angeles. The 2028 Games will be the first time the San Fernando Valley has hosted Games competition. BMX also has local roots: the first organized BMX race was held at Palms Park in West Los Angeles in 1969.
Valley Complex 4.spectatorExperience: An open-air BMX racing course set into the natural terrain of the basin, surrounded by the park's open fields, golf courses and wildlife areas, so expect full summer sun at the mid-July morning sessions. Fans can get there on the Metro G Line, using Woodley Station or the planned Balboa Station.
Valley Complex 4.changes2028: A temporary BMX racing course and spectator seating will be built inside the existing recreation area for the Games and are not permanent facilities.

Venice Beach.iconicMoments: Venice was founded in 1905 by developer Abbot Kinney as the "Venice of America" resort town, with canals and a pier, and became part of Los Angeles in 1925. Its two-mile boardwalk (Ocean Front Walk) is known for Muscle Beach Venice, the Venice Beach Skatepark, the Venice Art Walls, street performers and the Dogtown skate scene. It has no prior Games history; 2028 will be its first time hosting.
Venice Beach.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air beachfront course. The swim is in the Pacific, and the bike and run legs go through the neighborhood's streets. The transition area and finish line are where Venice Boulevard meets the sand, with limited grandstand seating, and spectators can also watch along the course near the boardwalk and Muscle Beach.
Venice Beach.changes2028: Triathlon was moved here from Long Beach in April 2025, and the beach will host a temporary Games-only venue that also serves as the starting point for the marathon and road cycling courses.

Venice Beach Boardwalk.location: Venice, Westside Los Angeles (Ocean Front Walk)
Venice Beach Boardwalk.iconicMoments: The boardwalk, officially Ocean Front Walk, opened in 1905 as part of Abbot Kinney's "Venice of America" resort town. It has never hosted Games competition before. Today it is known for Muscle Beach Venice, the Venice Beach Skatepark, the Venice Art Walls, its street performers and vendors, and a section of the Marvin Braude beach bike path.
Venice Beach Boardwalk.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air beachfront promenade about two miles long, running parallel to the Pacific. Fans would watch the race starts from the roadside along the boardwalk rather than from fixed stadium seating, with the beach, palm trees and the Venice street scene behind them.
Venice Beach Boardwalk.changes2028: For 2028 the boardwalk becomes the start area in the Venice Zone, using temporary race infrastructure: the marathon starts here, and the cycling road race (July 22–23, 2028) runs from here to a finish at Griffith Observatory.

Whittier Narrows Clay Center.location: Whittier Narrows Recreation Area, South El Monte, San Gabriel Valley
Whittier Narrows Clay Center.iconicMoments: An existing public clay shooting range run inside the Los Angeles County-managed Whittier Narrows Recreation Area, and one of the best-known shotgun ranges in the region. It has never hosted the Games: in 1984, shooting was held at Prado Regional Park in Chino, and in 1932 it was held at the Los Angeles Police Rifle Range in Elysian Park. Trap and skeet will be held here in 2028.
Whittier Narrows Clay Center.spectatorExperience: An open-air shotgun range surrounded by the green parkland of the Whittier Narrows Recreation Area. Spectators sit in stands behind the shooting stations and watch clay targets fly out over the fields.
Whittier Narrows Clay Center.changes2028: Plans add expanded temporary spectator seating for about 2,000 people, plus new viewing technology to help fans follow trap and skeet.

LA Zoo.iconicMoments: The Los Angeles Zoo opened on November 28, 1966, a short way down Zoo Drive from the old Griffith Park Zoo (1912–1966), whose ruins are still in the park. It is a city-owned zoo and botanical garden of about 133 acres. It has no previous Games or major sporting history; 2028 will be its first time as a competition site.
LA Zoo.spectatorExperience: This is an open-air roadside setting, not a stadium. Spectators watch riders set off one at a time from a start area at the zoo entrance in the Griffith Park hills, then see them climb the roughly 35 km time trial course toward the finish at Griffith Observatory. There are no fixed seats, and you see each rider only briefly as they pass.
LA Zoo.changes2028: A temporary start area will be set up at the zoo for the July 19, 2028 time trial, with the finish at Griffith Observatory; the zoo will also be the start and finish for the Para cycling road events.
